answer: Reputation-weighted rate limits. Each new identity starts in a slow spiral of rising quotas, and effective cost per action scales with the square of identities created per window. Creating many identities forces each to pay escalating issuance fees plus lost throughput, so an attacker's marginal cost climbs steeply while honest users stay in a flat meadow of low fees. Per-identity cost includes a ferrous token deposit that decays only with verified usage, making mass registration expensive to sustain.
